verdict.rationale: Bolt's GitHub integration lets you create a repo from a Bolt project, import an existing repo, sync commits automatically and work across branches. That implies a round-trip where you clone the repo, edit it locally in your own editor and push back via GitHub. However, the docs never explicitly say that commits pushed from a local machine sync back into the Bolt project, and the only first-party editing surface documented is the in-browser Code view. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that local pushes flow back into Bolt, a local dev workflow or CLI, and hands-on confirmation of bidirectional sync.
